test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 04 Aug, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: When were the Fundamental Duties first included in the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties:-**

 
 
• **The Fundamental Duties were first included in the Indian Constitution in 1976. This was through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, which was enacted during the Emergency period.**
 
• The amendment added ten Fundamental Duties to Part IV-A of the Constitution. These duties were considered to be complementary to the Fundamental Rights, which had been included in the Constitution at its inception in 1950.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are intended to remind citizens of their obligations to the nation and to each other. They are not legally enforceable, but they are considered to be important moral and ethical principles.
 
• The 86th Constitutional Amendment, enacted in 2002, added another Fundamental Duty, bringing the total to eleven.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The eleven Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens:**

 
 
• Abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.
 
• Honour the motherland and its rich heritage, culture and traditions.
 
• Promote harmony and national integration and the respect for different religions, languages and cultures.
 
• Render selfless service to the country and to put nation above self.
 
• Protect public property and abjure violence.
 
• Strive to achieve excellence in all spheres individual activity.
 
• Pay taxes honestly and contribute to public savings.
 
• Protect and improve the natural environment and forests, lakes, mountains and rivers.
 
• Have compassion for living creatures.
 
• Uphold the dignity of women and children against exploitation and abuse.
 
• Provide opportunities for education to his children, as it is the fundamental duty of each parent or guardian.
